cohort: 242,342 singletons born between 1999-2014 at a single tertiary medical center
finding: Offspring of mothers who smoked during pregnancy had higher rates of GI-related hospitalizations and an increased risk for inflammatory bowel disease.
mod_finding: While this study controlled for mode of delivery as a confounder, it did not examine mode of delivery as a primary or secondary outcome.
birth_weight: Mentioned as a confounder, but specific values not provided
